classes.objetivo: Seguir conversaciones rápidas con voces que se solapan, frases que se quedan a medias y cambios bruscos de turno, y reconstruir la idea de cada hablante sin perder el hilo.

vocabulario.es: lograr decir algo (cuando otro no para)

ensenanza.en: When excited friends overlap, sentences trail off halfway and the listener has to rebuild the meaning from whatever is left.
ensenanza.es: Cuando unos amigos entusiasmados se solapan, las frases se quedan a medias y el oyente tiene que reconstruir el significado con lo que queda.
ensenanza.nota: Overlap describe voces que suenan a la vez; trail off, una frase que se apaga sin terminar.

ensenanza.en: Hang on, sorry to interrupt, but I thought the meeting had been moved to Friday, not to Thursday.
ensenanza.es: Espera, perdona que interrumpa, pero pensaba que la reunión se había pasado al viernes, no al jueves.
ensenanza.nota: Hang on frena la conversación; sorry to interrupt pide permiso para cortar.

ensenanza.en: We all talk over each other and interrupt constantly, so I sometimes lose the thread of what anyone is saying.
ensenanza.es: Todos hablamos encima unos de otros y nos interrumpimos sin parar, así que a veces pierdo el hilo de lo que dice cada uno.
ensenanza.nota: Lose the thread = perder el hilo; talk over each other = hablar a la vez.

ensenanza.en: Whenever Tom is on a roll, nobody can get a word in edgeways, so we chime in early and our voices overlap.
ensenanza.es: Cuando Tom está lanzado, nadie logra meter una palabra, así que intervenimos pronto y nuestras voces se solapan.
ensenanza.nota: Get a word in edgeways = lograr decir algo cuando otro no para; chime in = intervenir de forma espontánea.

ensenanza.en: Anyway, as I was saying, let us switch to the budget before the room gets too noisy to hear properly.
ensenanza.es: En fin, como iba diciendo, pasemos al presupuesto antes de que la sala se ponga demasiado ruidosa para oír bien.
ensenanza.nota: As I was saying retoma lo dicho antes; switch to + tema cambia de tema a propósito.

ensenanza.en: Sorry, did I cut in? Go ahead; I did not mean to interrupt, I simply got carried away.
ensenanza.es: Perdona, ¿me metí en medio? Adelante; no quería interrumpir, simplemente me dejé llevar.
ensenanza.nota: Go ahead devuelve el turno a quien fue interrumpido; cut in = meterse a mitad de una frase ajena.

explicacion.texto: En una conversación rápida la gente se interrumpe, termina las frases de otros y habla a la vez. En el texto se marca con un guion (—) y en el audio se nota porque las frases se quedan a medias. Tu trabajo es reconstruir la idea aunque falten trozos: fíjate en quién habla, en las formas reducidas (gonna, dunno) y en las fórmulas de turno: hang on (espera), go ahead (sigue), as I was saying (como iba diciendo). Si pierdes el hilo, no busques cada palabra: recupera primero la idea principal.

formula.texto: Are we gonna book the room or—

erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Para pedir perdón antes de hacer algo se usa sorry to + verbo; «por interrumpir» no es for + verbo base.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Can you repeat me the last part?
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Can you repeat the last part?
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Repeat no lleva complemento de persona como «repíteme»: se dice repeat the last part o say that again.

situacion.contexto: Mia y Tom organizan una cena y hablan tan rápido que a veces se pisan.

dialogo.texto: So are we going to book the room for Friday or—
dialogo.traduccion: Entonces, ¿reservamos la sala para el viernes o—?

dialogo.texto: Already did. I booked it yesterday, but— hang on, it says Saturday.
dialogo.traduccion: Ya lo hice. La reservé ayer, pero— espera, pone sábado.

dialogo.texto: Saturday? No, no, we said Friday! Sorry, go ahead.
dialogo.traduccion: ¿Sábado? ¡No, no, dijimos viernes! Perdona, sigue.

dialogo.texto: Right, I will change it. Sorry, I talked over you.
dialogo.traduccion: Claro, lo cambiaré. Perdona, te hablé encima.

item.consigna: ¿Qué pasó con la reserva de la sala?

opciones.es: Tom la hizo, pero para el sábado en lugar del viernes.
Nadie ha reservado todavía la sala para la cena.
Mia la reservó para el sábado por error.

item.feedback: Tom dice «I booked it yesterday, but it says Saturday»: reservó, pero con el día equivocado.

guiada.consigna: ¿Qué función cumple «hang on» en esta escena?
guiada.feedback: Hang on frena a Tom para comprobar un dato; no le cede el turno (eso sería go ahead) ni cambia de tema.
guiada.texto: Tom was halfway through giving the schedule when Mia said hang on, because the date he had just read out did not match the one on the invitation.
opciones: It stops the talk so that she can check something.
It invites Tom to carry on with the rest of his explanation.
It changes the subject to the invitation itself.
guiada.pista: Es una fórmula para frenar, no para seguir.

guiada.consigna: Completa: «Perdona, no quería interrumpir; adelante, por favor.»
guiada.feedback: Go ahead es la fórmula para devolver el turno a quien se interrumpió.
guiada.texto: Sorry, I did not mean to interrupt you. Please ___ ahead; I would like to hear the rest of your idea.
guiada.pista: Verbo de movimiento de dos letras.

guiada.consigna: Relaciona cada fórmula con la función que cumple en la conversación.
guiada.feedback: Cada fórmula gestiona el turno de una manera distinta: frenar, ceder, retomar o pedir permiso.
guiada.pista: Piensa en si la fórmula quita o da la palabra.

practica.consigna: Escucha y elige cómo reacciona Leo cuando Ana habla por encima de él.
practica.feedback: Leo no discute ni pide aclaraciones: espera y retoma su idea justo donde la había dejado.
practica.audio: Leo started to say that the train left at nine, but Ana, talking over him, insisted that it was ten past. Leo did not argue. He simply waited, then picked up where he had stopped and said that the platform had changed.
opciones: He waits and then returns to his own point.
He asks Ana to say the time again so that he can check it.
He repeats the time more loudly until she agrees.

practica.consigna: ¿Qué deduces de la última frase de Tom?
practica.feedback: Tom rechazó otras invitaciones para el viernes porque creía que la fiesta era ese día; su frase anterior, cortada por Sara, iba en esa dirección.
practica.texto: Tom: Are you coming on Friday or— Mia: Saturday, I told you Saturday. Tom: Sorry, hang on, I thought the party was— Sara: Saturday. Everybody knows it is Saturday. Tom: Then I have already turned down two other invitations for Friday.
opciones: That he had kept Friday free because he thought the party was then.
That he would now rather go to one of the other parties.
That he had turned down the invitations because Mia asked him to.

practica.consigna: Ordena: «Pierdo el hilo cuando todos hablan encima de los demás.»
practica.feedback: When + sujeto + verbo explica cuándo ocurre: talk over each other describe el solapamiento.
practica.respuesta: I lose the thread when everyone talks over each other

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha y elige qué dato de Sara cambiaba los planes de la fiesta.
evaluacion.feedback: El dato de Sara es la fecha del departamento (sábado, no viernes); el pedido del pastel es de Mia y el pago de Carlos.
evaluacion.audio: Four flatmates were planning a surprise party, and nobody finished a sentence. Mia started to say that the cake should be ordered by Thursday, but Tom cut in to ask who was paying, and Carlos, talking over both of them, said he could pay if nobody minded waiting until the end of the month. Sara tried to get a word in edgeways, because the flat would be free only on Saturday, not on Friday, which changed everything. Mia laughed, said hang on, as she was saying, the cake came first, and asked Sara to go ahead. Sara repeated the date, and everyone agreed, although Carlos was still not sure about the money.
opciones: The flat would not be free until Saturday.
The cake could not be ordered before Thursday.
Carlos could pay only at the end of the month.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha y elige qué sugiere la reacción final de Carlos.
evaluacion.feedback: «Still not sure about the money» indica que para él el tema del dinero seguía pendiente, aunque aceptó la fecha.
evaluacion.audio: Four flatmates were planning a surprise party, and nobody finished a sentence. Mia started to say that the cake should be ordered by Thursday, but Tom cut in to ask who was paying, and Carlos, talking over both of them, said he could pay if nobody minded waiting until the end of the month. Sara tried to get a word in edgeways, because the flat would be free only on Saturday, not on Friday, which changed everything. Mia laughed, said hang on, as she was saying, the cake came first, and asked Sara to go ahead. Sara repeated the date, and everyone agreed, although Carlos was still not sure about the money.
opciones: That the question of the money was still open.
That he could not attend the party on Saturday.
That he preferred to leave the planning to the others.

evaluacion.consigna: Completa: «Perdona, ¿me metí en medio justo cuando ibas a explicarlo?»
evaluacion.feedback: Cut in (o chime in, jump in) describe meterse en una frase ajena antes de que termine.
evaluacion.texto: Sorry, did I ___ in just as you were about to explain? Please, go ahead; I will wait for you to finish.

evaluacion.consigna: Ordena: «Como iba diciendo, nadie había reservado la sala para el viernes.»
evaluacion.feedback: As I was saying retoma lo dicho antes; el resto da el contenido con el pasado perfecto had booked.
evaluacion.respuesta: As I was saying nobody had booked the room for Friday

repaso.consigna: ¿Qué da a entender esta pauta de reacciones?
repaso.feedback: Nadie responde: cambian de tema, se excusan y siguen con otra cosa, señal de que evitan la tarea de contárselo a Leo; no hay acuerdo previo ni problema de ruido.
repaso.texto: Sara asked who was going to tell Leo that his proposal had been turned down. Nobody said no. Carlos changed the subject, Mia suddenly remembered an appointment, and Tom carried on talking about the menu as if the question had never been asked.
opciones: That none of them wanted to take on that job.
That they had all agreed earlier who would do it.
That they had not heard Sara's question over the noise.

repaso.consigna: Escucha y elige qué hace Sara después de que todos se ríen.
repaso.feedback: Sara espera y retoma su explicación con «as I was saying».
repaso.audio: Sara was about to explain the new rota when Leo chimed in with a joke about the office coffee, and three people laughed at once. Sara waited, smiled and said, as I was saying, the rota starts on Monday.
opciones: She goes back to explaining the new rota.
She laughs along and drops the subject.
She asks Leo to start the explanation again.

repaso.consigna: Completa: «Con tanto ruido, perdí el hilo de la conversación.»
repaso.feedback: Lose the thread es la colocación para perder el hilo de lo que se está diciendo.
repaso.texto: The restaurant was so noisy that everybody spoke at once, and halfway through dinner I lost the ___ of the conversation completely.

classes.objetivo: Comprender a hablantes de India, Nigeria, Irlanda y Australia reconociendo rasgos de léxico y gramática propios de cada variedad del inglés, y captar la idea general sin descifrar cada palabra.

vocabulario.es: dar un toque de llamada (inglés de Nigeria)

ensenanza.en: Because a regional variety is a full system, not a mistake, colloquial words such as arvo or heaps are perfectly normal there.
ensenanza.es: Como una variedad regional es un sistema completo y no un error, palabras coloquiales como arvo o heaps son perfectamente normales allí.
ensenanza.nota: Colloquial = propio del habla cotidiana; arvo (tarde) y heaps (un montón) son rasgos del inglés australiano.

ensenanza.en: In India a colleague may ask you to prepone tomorrow's meeting, which means moving it earlier, the opposite of postpone.
ensenanza.es: En la India un colega puede pedirte que adelantes la reunión de mañana, lo que significa pasarla a una hora más temprana, lo contrario de postpone.
ensenanza.nota: Prepone es típico del inglés de la India: se forma por analogía con postpone.

ensenanza.en: How far is a friendly greeting in Nigeria, and flash me means ring once and hang up so that I call you back.
ensenanza.es: How far es un saludo amistoso en Nigeria, y flash me significa llamar una vez y colgar para que yo devuelva la llamada.
ensenanza.nota: How far? no pregunta por la distancia: equivale a «¿qué tal?»; flash funciona como verbo.

ensenanza.en: An Irish speaker who says I am grand is fine, not big, and I am after finishing means that I have just finished.
ensenanza.es: Un irlandés que dice I am grand está bien, no es grande, y I am after finishing significa que acabo de terminar.
ensenanza.nota: Grand = estupendo, bien; be after + -ing expresa una acción recién terminada.

ensenanza.en: An Australian might say I reckon we have heaps of time this arvo, and listeners soon pick up on these words.
ensenanza.es: Un australiano podría decir Creo que tenemos un montón de tiempo esta tarde, y quien escucha pronto se da cuenta de estas palabras.
ensenanza.nota: Reckon = creer; pick up on = percibir algo que no se dice de forma explícita.

ensenanza.en: Colloquial speech in every variety carries a distinctive lilt, and if you get the gist you can manage without every word.
ensenanza.es: El habla coloquial de cada variedad tiene una cadencia característica, y si captas la idea general puedes arreglártelas sin entender cada palabra.
ensenanza.nota: Get the gist = entender lo esencial; lilt es el ritmo melódico de un acento.

explicacion.texto: El inglés se habla en decenas de países y cada variedad regional tiene su acento, su ritmo y algunas palabras propias, aunque comparte casi toda la gramática. Aquí practicas el léxico y las estructuras: prepone (India, «adelantar»), how far? y flash me (Nigeria), grand y «I am after + -ing» (Irlanda), arvo, reckon y heaps (Australia). Como la voz de la app es sintética, el acento lo irás afinando con hablantes reales. Si no entiendes una palabra, deduce por el contexto y quédate con la idea general.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: I am after to finish my exams.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: I am after finishing my exams.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: En el inglés de Irlanda after va seguido de -ing: I am after finishing, no after to finish.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: We have heaps of times this arvo.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: We have heaps of time this arvo.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Time, cuando significa «tiempo disponible», es incontable: heaps of time, sin -s.

situacion.contexto: Leo trabaja con compañeros de otros países y le pide a Ana que le aclare dos expresiones.

dialogo.texto: My colleague in India asked me to prepone tomorrow's call, and I thought she wanted it later.
dialogo.traduccion: Mi colega de la India me pidió que adelantara la llamada de mañana, y pensé que la quería más tarde.

dialogo.texto: No, it is the opposite of postpone: she wants it earlier, at nine instead of ten.
dialogo.traduccion: No, es lo contrario de postpone: la quiere antes, a las nueve en vez de a las diez.

dialogo.texto: And in Ireland they say I am grand, which sounds like a boast.
dialogo.traduccion: Y en Irlanda dicen I am grand, que suena a presumir.

dialogo.texto: Not at all. It is colloquial for I am fine, so just get the gist and answer warmly.
dialogo.traduccion: Para nada. Es coloquial para «estoy bien», así que capta la idea general y responde con calidez.

opciones.es: Porque lo confundió con «postpone», que significa aplazar.
Porque es una palabra que solo se usa en Irlanda.
Porque su colega la pronunció con un acento muy marcado.

item.feedback: Leo pensó que su colega quería la llamada más tarde; Ana le aclara que prepone es lo contrario de postpone.

guiada.consigna: ¿Qué pide la colega de la India cuando escribe «prepone»?
guiada.feedback: Prepone es lo contrario de postpone: pasar la reunión a una hora más temprana, como explica el cliente que se une antes del almuerzo.
guiada.texto: Our colleague in India wrote: Could we prepone tomorrow's review to nine, so that the client can join us before lunch?
opciones: To hold the review earlier than planned.
To cancel the review until further notice.
To move the review to the afternoon.

guiada.consigna: Completa: «Estoy bien, gracias; acabo de terminar los exámenes.»
guiada.feedback: Grand significa «bien, estupendo» en el inglés de Irlanda, no «grande».
guiada.texto: Asked how she was, the Irish student smiled and said: I am ___, thanks; I am just after finishing my exams.
guiada.pista: Una palabra de cinco letras que aquí no significa «big».

guiada.consigna: Relaciona cada palabra con la variedad del inglés en la que es típica.
guiada.feedback: Cada rasgo pertenece a una variedad: prepone (India), flash (Nigeria), grand (Irlanda) y arvo (Australia).
guiada.pista: Piensa en una palabra de cada país del texto de la clase.

practica.consigna: Escucha y elige qué debe hacer Leo al llegar al aeropuerto.
practica.feedback: Flash her significa dar un toque de llamada: ella no puede pagar una llamada larga.
practica.audio: Leo's cousin in Lagos answered the phone with how far, and only afterwards did he realise that it was a greeting, not a question about distance. Later she asked him to flash her when he arrived at the airport, because she could not afford a long call.
opciones: Ring once and hang up.
Send her a long message.
Call and wait until she answers.

practica.consigna: ¿Qué dice la vecina irlandesa de Tom sobre sus resultados?
practica.feedback: I am after getting indica una acción recién terminada: acaba de recibir los resultados, y «not what I expected» muestra que son una decepción.
practica.texto: Tom asked his Irish neighbour how the exams went. She said: They were grand, although I am after getting my results and they are not what I expected.
opciones: She has only just got them, and they are a real disappointment.
She is waiting for them, and feels sure they will be good.
She got them a while ago, and they were better than expected.

practica.consigna: Ordena: «Creo que tendremos un montón de tiempo esta tarde.»
practica.feedback: Reckon = creer y heaps of time = un montón de tiempo, dos rasgos coloquiales del inglés australiano.
practica.respuesta: I reckon we will have heaps of time this arvo
aceptadas: We will have heaps of time this arvo I reckon

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha y elige para qué prometió Leo «flash» al narrador al llegar.
evaluacion.feedback: Flash me significa dar un toque de llamada: Leo avisará de que ha llegado sin gastar saldo en una llamada completa; el retraso y el cambio de hora no se mencionan en relación con flash.
evaluacion.audio: Last month I joined a project with colleagues in four countries, and the first call was a lesson in listening. Ana, in Pune, asked whether we could prepone the next meeting to nine o'clock, and for a moment I thought she meant the opposite. Leo, in Lagos, opened with how far, which is simply hello, and promised to flash me when he arrived, because a proper call would eat up his credit. Mia, in Cork, said that she was grand, just after finishing her exams. Finally Tom, in Perth, reckoned there would be heaps of time this arvo. None of it was difficult once I stopped working out every word and started to get the gist.
opciones: To signal his arrival without paying for a proper call.
To warn him that the meeting would start late.
To confirm that the meeting had been moved earlier.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha y elige qué sugiere el narrador al final sobre cómo seguir una conversación.
evaluacion.feedback: Dice que todo fue fácil cuando dejó de descifrar cada palabra y captó la idea general.
evaluacion.audio: Last month I joined a project with colleagues in four countries, and the first call was a lesson in listening. Ana, in Pune, asked whether we could prepone the next meeting to nine o'clock, and for a moment I thought she meant the opposite. Leo, in Lagos, opened with how far, which is simply hello, and promised to flash me when he arrived, because a proper call would eat up his credit. Mia, in Cork, said that she was grand, just after finishing her exams. Finally Tom, in Perth, reckoned there would be heaps of time this arvo. None of it was difficult once I stopped working out every word and started to get the gist.
opciones: That getting the overall sense matters more than working out each word.
That colleagues should agree on one standard form before meetings.
That understanding comes only after years living in those countries.

evaluacion.consigna: Completa: «Mi colega de Perth dice que tendremos un montón de tiempo esta tarde.»
evaluacion.feedback: Heaps of + incontable es coloquial, típico del inglés australiano, como arvo.
evaluacion.texto: My colleague in Perth says that we will have ___ of time this arvo, so there is no need to hurry.

evaluacion.consigna: Empareja cada frase con la variedad y el significado que aporta.
evaluacion.feedback: Cada frase combina una variedad con su significado: adelantar, avisar con un toque, acabar de hacer algo y mucho tiempo.

repaso.consigna: ¿Qué actitud adopta el autor ante quien dice que esas variedades son incorrectas?
repaso.feedback: El autor recuerda que cada variedad tiene reglas coherentes y se entiende entre sus hablantes: la queja nace de un malentendido; no aconseja evitarlas ni propone enseñarlas antes que el estándar.
repaso.texto: Some learners complain that Indian, Nigerian or Irish English is wrong. They forget that every regional variety follows its own consistent rules, and that speakers who say prepone or am after finishing are being perfectly clear to one another.
opciones: He thinks the complaint overlooks how naturally language varies from one region to another.
He agrees with the learners and advises avoiding such forms in exams.
He argues that each variety should be taught in schools before any standard.

repaso.consigna: Escucha y elige cuándo debía llegar el paquete según la dependienta.
repaso.feedback: La dependienta dijo que llegaría «in the arvo», es decir, por la tarde; el comentario de la amiga sobre «heaps of time» no indica que tardara días.
repaso.audio: A shop assistant in Melbourne told me that the parcel would come in the arvo. Later a friend from Sydney said that she reckoned it would take heaps of time, so I waited and made some coffee. It arrived at four.
opciones: Later that same afternoon.
Early the next morning.
Within a few days.

repaso.consigna: Completa: «¿Podríamos adelantar la llamada una hora?»
repaso.feedback: Prepone es el verbo del inglés de la India para adelantar una cita; move también sirve, pero sin ese matiz regional.
repaso.texto: The call is fixed for ten, but the client is free earlier. Could we ___ the call by an hour, so that nobody has to stay late?

classes.objetivo: Deducir lo que el hablante quiere decir en diálogos cotidianos cuando la respuesta es indirecta, evasiva o muy cortés («Well… it is a bit pricey»), y leer entre líneas.

ensenanza.en: “Well, it is a bit pricey, so I will think about it” is a polite way of saying that the shopper will probably not buy.
ensenanza.es: «Bueno, es un poco caro, así que lo pensaré» es una forma cortés de decir que quien compra probablemente no comprará.
ensenanza.nota: Dice «es caro» pero quiere decir «probablemente no»; la pausa y a bit suavizan el rechazo.

ensenanza.en: “I suppose it could work” is what people say when they accept an idea without any enthusiasm at all.
ensenanza.es: «Supongo que podría funcionar» es lo que se dice cuando se acepta una idea sin ningún entusiasmo.
ensenanza.nota: I suppose suena a aceptar sin ganas: el hablante no está convencido.

ensenanza.en: Honest friends still try to let someone down gently, so a refusal often hides inside a compliment.
ensenanza.es: Los amigos sinceros también intentan rechazar con tacto, así que un rechazo suele esconderse dentro de un cumplido.
ensenanza.nota: Let someone down gently = rechazar sin herir; el «no» se disfraza de elogio.

ensenanza.en: “It is not exactly what the client wanted, but we will see” suggests real doubt, not a promise.
ensenanza.es: «No es exactamente lo que quería el cliente, pero ya veremos» sugiere una duda real, no una promesa.
ensenanza.nota: Not exactly equivale casi a «no»; we will see muestra dudas, no un compromiso.

ensenanza.en: You learn to read between the lines when someone hardly answers the question and quickly changes the subject.
ensenanza.es: Aprendes a leer entre líneas cuando alguien apenas responde a la pregunta y cambia rápido de tema.
ensenanza.nota: Hardly (apenas) y un cambio de tema son señales de una respuesta evasiva.

ensenanza.en: Honest speakers who beat around the bush are rarely lying; to put it mildly, they just dislike saying no.
ensenanza.es: Quienes se andan por las ramas rara vez mienten; por decirlo suavemente, simplemente les disgusta decir que no.
ensenanza.nota: Beat around the bush = no ir al grano; to put it mildly suaviza una crítica fuerte.

explicacion.titulo: Lo que se dice y lo que se quiere decir
explicacion.texto: En inglés cotidiano, sobre todo con cortesía, lo importante suele quedar sin decir. Una pausa («Well…»), un suavizador (a bit, I suppose, hardly) o una respuesta vaga (I will think about it, we will see) suelen significar «no» o «no me convence». Pregúntate qué esperaba el oyente y si la respuesta lo cumple; si evita decir sí o no, probablemente es un no amable. Leer entre líneas es notar lo que falta: «It is a bit pricey» casi nunca habla solo del precio.

patron.texto: Pausa + suavizador + respuesta vaga = rechazo amable:

formula.nota: suavizador: el «no» se disfraza de comentario

formula.texto: so I will think about it.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: He said me that it was a bit expensive.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: He told me that it was a bit expensive.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Con persona como complemento se usa told me, no said me: he told me / he said to me.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: It is not exactly cheap, no?
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: It is not exactly cheap, is it?
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: La coletilla «¿no?» se traduce con una question tag: is it? después de una frase negativa.

situacion.contexto: Sara y Carlos están en una tienda de ropa y Carlos le pregunta por una chaqueta azul.

dialogo.texto: Do you want to buy the blue jacket?
dialogo.traduccion: ¿Quieres comprar la chaqueta azul?

dialogo.texto: Well… it is a bit pricey, so I will think about it.
dialogo.traduccion: Bueno… es un poco cara, así que lo pensaré.

dialogo.texto: So, is that a yes?
dialogo.traduccion: Entonces, ¿es un sí?

dialogo.texto: To be honest, not exactly.
dialogo.traduccion: Siendo sincera, no exactamente.

opciones.es: Que probablemente no va a comprar la chaqueta.
Que quiere comprar la chaqueta ahora mismo.
Que no ha entendido la pregunta de Carlos.

item.feedback: Sara evita decir que sí («a bit pricey», «I will think about it») y al final lo confirma con «not exactly».

guiada.feedback: La pausa y un adjetivo vago («certainly different») suavizan una opinión poco entusiasta.
guiada.texto: Do you like my new coat? — Well… it is certainly different.
opciones: She is not impressed but avoids saying so.
She is delighted and wants to copy it.
She did not notice that anything had changed.
guiada.pista: Las pausas y los adjetivos vagos suelen suavizar una crítica.

guiada.consigna: Completa: «Supongo que podría funcionar, aunque yo habría elegido otro.»
guiada.feedback: I suppose it could work expresa una aceptación sin entusiasmo: la frase siguiente lo confirma.
guiada.texto: Is the new timetable acceptable? — I ___ it could work, although I would have chosen another.
guiada.pista: Verbo de pensamiento que aquí significa «imagino».

guiada.consigna: Relaciona cada respuesta con lo que probablemente quiere decir el hablante.
guiada.feedback: Cada respuesta indirecta esconde un mensaje: rechazo por el precio, un no amable, aceptación fría o falta de compromiso.
pares: Well… it is a bit pricey.
guiada.pista: Pregúntate qué respuesta evita decir sí o no.

practica.consigna: Escucha y elige qué opina Mia probablemente de la música.
practica.feedback: Mia elogia solo lo secundario (las luces y la sala) y cambia de tema: señal de que la música no la convenció; no critica el sonido de la sala, que alaba.
practica.audio: After the concert, Tom asked Mia how the band had been. She took a moment, said that the lights were lovely and the hall was very comfortable, and then asked whether they should get something to eat. Tom nodded slowly and did not ask about the singing again.
opciones: She was not impressed by the music itself.
She loved every song the band played.
She thought the sound in the hall was poor.

practica.consigna: ¿Qué piensa realmente la autora del borrador?
practica.feedback: Con «I suppose», «hardly» y «let us see» suaviza una opinión clara: el borrador no está listo; no lo considera casi terminado ni pide solo una segunda opinión.
practica.texto: Thanks for sending the draft. There are a few things I suppose we could look at again, and I hardly think it is ready for the client yet, but let us see how the week goes.
opciones: It needs substantial work before anyone outside the team sees it.
It is nearly ready and needs only small changes.
It is fine, and she only wants a second opinion first.

practica.consigna: Ordena: «Supongo que podríamos intentarlo, pero no me convence.»
practica.feedback: I suppose introduce la aceptación sin ganas y but I am not convinced revela la duda real.
practica.respuesta: I suppose we could try it but I am not convinced

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha y elige qué quiere decir Mia con «I will think about it».
evaluacion.feedback: Mia deja la lámpara en el estante y se va hacia la puerta: «I will think about it» es aquí una forma cortés de decir que probablemente no la comprará.
evaluacion.audio: At the garden centre, Mia held up a lamp and asked Tom whether it was any good. Tom looked at the price tag and said that it was a bit pricey, but certainly bright. When Tom asked whether she was going to buy it, Mia said that she would think about it, put the lamp back on the shelf and headed for the door. Outside, Tom admitted that he could hardly say he loved the colour either, and they both laughed. The assistant, who had heard everything, pretended to tidy a shelf.
opciones: That she is probably not going to buy the lamp at all.
That she will buy it as soon as Tom approves the colour.
That she must first ask Tom to lend her the money.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha y elige qué insinúa Tom con «I could hardly say I loved the colour».
evaluacion.feedback: Hardly suaviza una crítica: Tom no está entusiasmado con el color, y ese «either» conecta su opinión con la reticencia de Mia, lo que explica que ambos se rían.
evaluacion.audio: At the garden centre, Mia held up a lamp and asked Tom whether it was any good. Tom looked at the price tag and said that it was a bit pricey, but certainly bright. When Tom asked whether she was going to buy it, Mia said that she would think about it, put the lamp back on the shelf and headed for the door. Outside, Tom admitted that he could hardly say he loved the colour either, and they both laughed. The assistant, who had heard everything, pretended to tidy a shelf.
opciones: That he is not very keen on the colour either, like Mia.
That he liked the colour but hid it to be polite.
That he would have preferred a cheaper lamp of the same colour.

evaluacion.consigna: Completa: «Para ser sincero, todavía no he tenido tiempo de leerlo.»
evaluacion.feedback: To be honest introduce algo incómodo: aquí, que el informe sigue sin leer.
evaluacion.texto: Did you read my report? — To be ___, I have not had time yet, but I will look at it tonight.

evaluacion.consigna: Ordena: «Sinceramente, no es exactamente lo que yo pedí.»
evaluacion.feedback: To be honest avisa de algo incómodo y not exactly suaviza la negación.
evaluacion.respuesta: To be honest that is not exactly what I asked for

repaso.consigna: ¿Qué es más probable que haga la autora del mensaje?
repaso.feedback: Los elogios, «very busy» y «I will check my diary» son la forma educada de preparar un rechazo; no acepta aunque diga que le gustaría ir, ni pide cambiar la fecha.
repaso.texto: Thanks so much for the invitation. It sounds lovely, and I would hate to miss seeing everyone. Things are very busy at work at the moment, but I will check my diary and let you know.
opciones: Decline the invitation, but in a polite and gentle way.
Accept, because she says she would hate to miss everyone.
Ask the hosts to change the date to suit her.

repaso.consigna: Escucha y elige por qué Leo dejó de sonreír.
repaso.feedback: Elogio vago, «when the budget allowed» y «keep up the good work» son señales de que la propuesta no será aprobada; Leo lo deduce y cierra el archivo para siempre.
repaso.audio: The manager told Leo that his proposal was interesting, that the team would look at it when the budget allowed, and that he should keep up the good work. Leo thanked him warmly, but as he walked back to his desk he stopped smiling and closed the proposal file for good.
opciones: He understood that the proposal would probably never be approved anyway.
He realised that the budget had already been spent on something else.
He was annoyed that the manager had not read the proposal.

repaso.consigna: Completa: «Por decirlo suavemente, el lanzamiento no salió como estaba previsto.»
repaso.feedback: To put it mildly suaviza una valoración muy negativa: en realidad fue un fracaso.
repaso.texto: To put it ___, the launch did not go as planned; the client left early and nobody has called since.

classes.objetivo: Tomar notas de una charla breve y resumirlas con tres ideas principales, dos detalles y una conclusión, atribuyendo lo dicho y sin inventar datos.

ensenanza.en: A good lecturer will draw attention to the turning points, so listen for signals such as first, however and in short, and keep track of how many points she promises.
ensenanza.es: Un buen conferenciante llamará la atención sobre los puntos de giro, así que escucha señales como first, however e in short, y lleva la cuenta de cuántos puntos promete.
ensenanza.nota: Keep track of = llevar la cuenta; las señales del orador (first, however, in short) marcan la estructura que debes apuntar.

ensenanza.en: According to the lecturer, a key point is that shade cools streets; she went on to give a telling detail: five degrees.
ensenanza.es: Según la conferenciante, un punto clave es que la sombra refresca las calles; continuó dando un detalle revelador: cinco grados.
ensenanza.nota: According to atribuye la idea; went on to + verbo añade un dato concreto que respalda el punto.

ensenanza.en: Sensible students jot down keywords and numbers, leaving out whole sentences, because the lecturer will not wait for them.
ensenanza.es: Los estudiantes sensatos anotan rápido palabras clave y cifras, sin frases enteras, porque el conferenciante no esperará.
ensenanza.nota: Jot down = anotar de prisa y en pocas palabras; take notes es la expresión general para tomar apuntes.

ensenanza.en: A recurring theme, such as how firms recruit people, links the three points that the lecturer outlined, so note it once.
ensenanza.es: Un tema recurrente, como la forma en que las empresas captan personal, une los tres puntos que expuso el conferenciante, así que anótalo una vez.
ensenanza.nota: Outlined + número de puntos anuncia la estructura; a recurring theme conecta ideas repartidas.

ensenanza.en: By way of illustration, she described one street where two thousand trees were planted; you can summarise it in a single line.
ensenanza.es: A modo de ilustración, describió una calle donde se plantaron dos mil árboles; puedes resumirlo en una sola línea.
ensenanza.nota: By way of illustration introduce un ejemplo; summarise = resumir (resume en inglés significa «reanudar»).

ensenanza.en: When you summarise, report what was said, not what you think, and close with in short followed by one sentence.
ensenanza.es: Cuando resumes, cuenta lo que se dijo, no lo que piensas, y cierra con in short seguido de una frase.
ensenanza.nota: Un resumen fiel separa lo dicho de tu opinión y termina con la conclusión.

explicacion.texto: Al escuchar una charla, apunta solo lo esencial: el tema, dos o tres ideas principales, algún dato concreto (cifras, nombres) y la conclusión. Las señales del orador (first, however, in short) te guían. Para resumir, atribuye lo que se dijo (The lecturer outlined…, According to her…, She went on to…), reformula con tus palabras y cierra con In short o To summarise. Un resumen fiel no incluye datos inventados ni tu opinión. Ojo: resume en inglés significa «reanudar», no «resumir».

formula.nota: atribuye la idea a la fuente

formula.texto: a key point is the price.
She went on to give a telling detail:

filas.texto: According to her, a key point…
went on to / by way of illustration
She went on to give a telling detail.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: The lecturer said us three reasons.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: The lecturer told us three reasons.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Said no lleva persona directamente: se dice told us o said to us.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Resuming, shared bikes are cheap and healthy.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: To summarise, shared bikes are cheap and healthy.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Resume significa «reanudar». Para resumir se usa to summarise o in short.

situacion.contexto: Ana no pudo ir a la charla de la mañana sobre los árboles en las ciudades y Leo le cuenta sus apuntes.

dialogo.texto: What did the lecturer say about trees in cities?
dialogo.traduccion: ¿Qué dijo la conferenciante sobre los árboles en las ciudades?

dialogo.texto: She outlined three reasons. According to her, a key point is that shade cools the streets.
dialogo.traduccion: Expuso tres razones. Según ella, un punto clave es que la sombra refresca las calles.

dialogo.texto: Did she give a telling detail?
dialogo.traduccion: ¿Dio algún detalle revelador?

dialogo.texto: Yes, by way of illustration, she said that shade can make a street five degrees cooler.
dialogo.traduccion: Sí, a modo de ilustración, dijo que la sombra puede hacer una calle cinco grados más fresca.

item.consigna: ¿Qué ejemplo dio la conferenciante, según Leo?

opciones.es: Que la sombra puede enfriar una calle cinco grados.
Que los árboles duplican el precio de las casas cercanas.
Que plantar árboles cuesta cinco euros por calle.

item.feedback: Leo cita el detalle: «shade can make a street five degrees cooler».

guiada.consigna: ¿Qué debe ir principalmente en tus notas durante una charla?
guiada.feedback: Con un orador rápido, lo útil son las cifras, los nombres y la idea de cada parte; copiar frases enteras te hace perder el hilo.
guiada.texto: You are listening to a twenty-minute talk on shared bikes. The lecturer speaks quickly, gives many figures and names, and moves on before you have finished writing.
opciones: Numbers, names and the main point of each section.
Every sentence exactly as the lecturer says it.
Your own opinion of each idea as it is mentioned.
guiada.pista: Piensa en lo que podrás reconstruir después con pocas palabras.

guiada.consigna: Completa: «Según la conferenciante, el beneficio clave es el precio.»
guiada.feedback: According to atribuye la idea a la fuente: es la señal básica de un resumen fiel.
guiada.texto: ___ to the lecturer, the key benefit of shared bikes is the price, and she went on to give a detail: one dollar per half hour.
guiada.pista: Dos palabras en total; la primera empieza por a.

guiada.consigna: Ordena: «Continuó dando un detalle revelador sobre el coste.»
guiada.feedback: Went on to + verbo añade un dato concreto después de la idea principal.
guiada.respuesta: She went on to give a telling detail about the cost
guiada.pista: El sujeto es she y el verbo frasal va antes del infinitivo.

practica.consigna: Escucha y elige qué tema recurrente destaca la conferenciante.
practica.feedback: El tema recurrente es que el sonido de fondo se tolera, pero el habla distrae; los auriculares son solo el ejemplo.
practica.audio: The lecturer began by saying that she would cover two topics. The first was noise in open offices; the second was light. On noise, she drew attention to a recurring theme in the research: people can get used to background sound, but they cannot easily ignore speech. By way of illustration, she mentioned a call centre where staff wore headphones.
opciones: People ignore background sound more easily than speech.
Open offices are always noisier than private rooms.
Staff in call centres dislike wearing headphones.

practica.consigna: Escucha y elige qué frase sería infiel en un resumen de la charla.
practica.feedback: La conferenciante dice que convienen a quien trabaja de día, que la asistencia se duplica en invierno y que un colegio los ofrece tres tardes por semana; nunca dice que sean mejores que los de día, así que esa frase sería infiel.
practica.audio: Night classes suit people who work during the day, the lecturer said, and attendance doubles in winter. For many adults they are the only option, and one college now runs them on three evenings a week.
opciones: Night classes are better than daytime classes.
Attendance doubles during the winter months.
At least one college runs them on three evenings a week.

practica.consigna: Completa: «Cuando tomes apuntes, escribe cifras, nombres y palabras clave.»
practica.feedback: Take notes es la colocación para tomar apuntes durante una charla.
practica.texto: When you take ___, write numbers, names and keywords; whole sentences will make you fall behind.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha la charla y resume tres ideas y dos detalles.
evaluacion.feedback: El resumen recoge las tres razones, al menos dos detalles, atribuye las ideas a la conferenciante, menciona el límite y cierra con una conclusión.
evaluacion.texto: Escucha la charla sobre la semana laboral de cuatro días (puedes oírla varias veces) y escribe un resumen en inglés de unas 170–250 palabras: tres ideas principales, dos detalles o ejemplos, un límite y una frase final. Atribuye las ideas a la conferenciante y no añadas datos que no oigas.
evaluacion.respuesta: The lecturer began by saying that she wanted to look at why some companies are trying a four-day working week, and she then outlined three main reasons. According to her, the first reason is that staff are more focused when a long weekend is coming, and the work done stayed the same at one firm in Bristol. The second reason is that sick days fell sharply, by about a third in a year. The third reason is that it became easier to recruit, because candidates see the shorter week as a sign of trust. By way of illustration, she described a company that reduced its hours from forty to thirty-two without cutting pay. She went on to draw attention to a limit: the change is not suitable for every kind of business, since hospitals and shops cannot simply close on Fridays. In short, the lecturer said that the four-day week works best where results, not hours, can be measured, and she did not suggest that every company should copy it.
aceptadas: The talk was about why some companies are trying a four-day week, and the speaker gave three main ideas. Firstly, staff seem to be more focused when a long weekend is coming, and at one firm in Bristol the work done did not change. Secondly, sick days fell: they went down by roughly a third in a year. Thirdly, it was easier to recruit people, since candidates see a shorter week as a sign of trust. As an example, she explained that a company cut its hours from forty to thirty-two and did not reduce pay. She also pointed out a limit: the idea does not suit every kind of business, because hospitals and shops cannot close on Fridays. To sum up, according to the lecturer, the four-day week is best where results can be measured rather than hours, although she did not say that every company should copy it.
evaluacion.audio: Good morning. Today I want to look at why some companies are trying a four-day working week. There are three main reasons. First, managers report that staff are more focused when they know a long weekend is coming, and one firm in Bristol found that the work done stayed the same after the change. Second, sick days fell sharply, by about a third in a year. Third, it became easier to recruit, because candidates see the shorter week as a sign of trust. By way of illustration, one company reduced its hours from forty to thirty-two without cutting pay. However, the change is not suitable for every kind of business; hospitals and shops cannot simply close on Fridays. In short, the four-day week works best where results can be measured, not hours.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha la charla y elige por qué menciona hospitales y tiendas.
evaluacion.feedback: Los hospitales y las tiendas son el ejemplo del límite: no pueden cerrar los viernes, así que el cambio no sirve para todos los sectores; la empresa que redujo horas y la confianza de los candidatos son otros ejemplos de la charla.
evaluacion.audio: Good morning. Today I want to look at why some companies are trying a four-day working week. There are three main reasons. First, managers report that staff are more focused when they know a long weekend is coming, and one firm in Bristol found that the work done stayed the same after the change. Second, sick days fell sharply, by about a third in a year. Third, it became easier to recruit, because candidates see the shorter week as a sign of trust. By way of illustration, one company reduced its hours from forty to thirty-two without cutting pay. However, the change is not suitable for every kind of business; hospitals and shops cannot simply close on Fridays. In short, the four-day week works best where results can be measured, not hours.
opciones: To show that the idea has limits in some kinds of business.
To illustrate a company that cut its hours without cutting pay.
To explain why candidates see a shorter week as a sign of trust.

evaluacion.consigna: Completa: «A modo de ilustración, una fábrica redujo sus horas.»
evaluacion.feedback: By way of illustration (o by way of example) introduce un caso concreto que respalda la idea.
evaluacion.texto: By way of ___, one company cut its hours from forty to thirty-two without reducing anybody's pay.

evaluacion.consigna: Ordena: «La conferenciante esbozó tres razones y continuó con un ejemplo.»
evaluacion.feedback: Outlined anuncia la estructura y went on to + verbo pasa al detalle.
evaluacion.respuesta: The lecturer outlined three reasons and went on to give an example

repaso.consigna: ¿Qué ha aprendido el autor de su experiencia con los apuntes?
repaso.feedback: Copiarlo todo no le sirvió para resumir; decide anotar solo cifras, nombres y un punto clave por parte, sin renunciar a tomar notas ni temer que el resumen pierda precisión.
repaso.texto: I copied every sentence the lecturer said, and my notes ran to six pages. Yet when I tried to summarise the talk, I could not tell which point mattered most. Next time I will write only the numbers, the names and one key point per section.
opciones: That choosing key points matters more than copying everything.
That he should have recorded the talk and skipped the notes.
That shorter notes will make the summary less accurate.

repaso.consigna: Escucha y elige qué insinúa la hablante sobre la fecha de apertura.
repaso.feedback: Menciona plazos incumplidos y atribuye la confianza al municipio con «in its own words»: se distancia de esa confianza y da a entender que duda de que se cumpla marzo.
repaso.audio: She said the new library would open in March, although the builders had already missed two deadlines, and then went on to say that the council was, in its own words, very confident.
opciones: That she doubts the date will be met.
That she trusts the council's confidence completely.
That the council has already changed the date.

repaso.consigna: Ordena: «Según la conferenciante, el punto clave es el coste.»
repaso.feedback: According to atribuye la idea y the key point is… presenta la idea principal.
repaso.respuesta: According to the lecturer the key point is the cost

classes.objetivo: Escuchar un episodio de pódcast, resumirlo con fidelidad, señalar una implicación y añadir una reacción propia con matiz, separando lo dicho, lo insinuado y lo que tú opinas.

vocabulario.es: lo que me llamó la atención

ensenanza.en: In this episode, the host asked her guest about working from home, and the guest came across as thoughtful rather than certain.
ensenanza.es: En este episodio, la presentadora preguntó a su invitada por el teletrabajo, y la invitada dio la impresión de ser reflexiva más que segura.
ensenanza.nota: Come across as + adjetivo describe la impresión que da alguien; host y guest organizan el episodio.

ensenanza.en: What struck me was that the guest never said the job was easy, although the host kept inviting her to.
ensenanza.es: Lo que me llamó la atención fue que la invitada nunca dijo que el trabajo fuera fácil, aunque la presentadora la invitaba a ello.
ensenanza.nota: What struck me was… introduce lo que te llamó la atención, incluso lo que no se dijo.

ensenanza.en: Her answers did not say so, yet they seem to imply that the change was harder than the host wanted to admit.
ensenanza.es: Sus respuestas no lo decían, pero parecen dar a entender que el cambio fue más difícil de lo que la presentadora quería admitir.
ensenanza.nota: Seem to imply señala una implicación sin afirmarla: lo insinuado no es lo dicho.

ensenanza.en: I do not want to read into a single pause too much, but the guest hesitated before every mention of the office.
ensenanza.es: No quiero interpretar de más una sola pausa, pero la invitada dudó antes de cada mención de la oficina.
ensenanza.nota: Read into = atribuir un significado que quizá no está; se usa con cautela.

ensenanza.en: To be fair, the host made a fair point, yet I take issue with the claim that the guest had simply changed her mind.
ensenanza.es: Para ser justos, la presentadora hizo una observación razonable, pero discrepo de que la invitada simplemente hubiera cambiado de opinión.
ensenanza.nota: To be fair reconoce lo bueno; take issue with introduce un desacuerdo concreto y educado.

ensenanza.en: A gut reaction is rarely the last word, so I agree up to a point and I would add one doubt about the episode.
ensenanza.es: Una reacción instintiva rara vez es la última palabra, así que estoy de acuerdo hasta cierto punto y añadiría una duda sobre el episodio.
ensenanza.nota: Up to a point matiza el acuerdo; I would add suma un punto propio sin negar lo anterior.

explicacion.texto: Un episodio de pódcast se trabaja en cuatro pasos: 1) toma notas mientras escuchas; 2) resume con fidelidad lo que se dijo (The host asked…, According to the guest…); 3) señala la implicación, lo que parece dar a entender sin decirlo (seem to imply: una respuesta corta o vaga puede decir más de lo que parece); 4) añade tu reacción con matiz (to be fair, I take issue with…, I would add…, up to a point). Mantén separadas las tres capas: lo dicho, lo insinuado y lo que opinas tú.

patron.texto: Resumen fiel + implicación + reacción con matiz:

formula.texto: According to the guest, it depends.
Her answer seemed to imply a doubt.
To be fair, I agree up to a point,
but I would add one doubt.

filas.texto: According to the guest, it depends.
Her answer seemed to imply a doubt.
to be fair / up to a point
To be fair, I agree up to a point.
I would add / take issue with

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: They talk about the work from home.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: They talk about working from home.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Para la actividad en general se usa el gerundio: working from home, no the work from home.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: I was surprised for her answer.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: I was surprised by her answer.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Con surprised el agente se introduce con by: surprised by her answer.

situacion.contexto: Mia y Tom acaban de oír un episodio de pódcast sobre el teletrabajo y lo comentan.

dialogo.texto: What struck me was that the guest never said working from home was easy.
dialogo.traduccion: Lo que me llamó la atención fue que la invitada nunca dijo que trabajar en casa fuera fácil.

dialogo.texto: I noticed that too. Her answers seem to imply that it can be lonely.
dialogo.traduccion: Yo también lo noté. Sus respuestas parecen dar a entender que puede ser solitario.

dialogo.texto: To be fair, she also mentioned the benefits, and she came across as careful.
dialogo.traduccion: Para ser justos, también mencionó los beneficios, y dio la impresión de ser cuidadosa.

dialogo.texto: True, but I take issue with one thing: not everyone has a quiet room.
dialogo.traduccion: Cierto, pero discrepo en una cosa: no todo el mundo tiene una habitación tranquila.

item.consigna: Según Tom, ¿qué insinuó la invitada sin decirlo?

opciones.es: Que trabajar en casa puede resultar solitario.
Que trabajar en casa es imposible para la mayoría.
Que los beneficios superan claramente a los problemas.

item.feedback: Tom dice que sus respuestas «seem to imply that it can be lonely»: lo insinúa sin afirmarlo.

guiada.consigna: Separa lo dicho de lo insinuado: ¿qué deja entrever la directora?
guiada.feedback: Cumplir lo pedido y añadir «we will see» no promete nada: insinúa dudas sobre si el equipo está listo.
guiada.texto: Asked whether her team was ready for the launch, the manager said: We have done everything the client asked, and we will see.
opciones: That she doubts the team is ready.
That the client asked for far too much.
That the team finished the work early.
guiada.pista: Fíjate en lo que no promete.

guiada.consigna: Completa: «Lo que me llamó la atención fue que la invitada nunca dijera que fuera fácil.»
guiada.feedback: What struck me was… introduce lo que te llamó la atención, aunque sea algo que no se dijo.
guiada.texto: What ___ me was that the guest never said working from home was easy, even when the host asked her twice.

guiada.consigna: Relaciona cada frase con la capa del comentario a la que pertenece.
guiada.feedback: Cada frase ocupa una capa distinta: lo dicho, lo insinuado, la reacción propia y lo que tú añades.
pares: The host asked whether it is better.
Her answer seemed to imply a doubt.
To be fair, I agree up to a point.
I would add that not everyone has a quiet room.
guiada.pista: Pregúntate si la frase cuenta, sugiere u opina.

practica.consigna: Escucha y elige qué insinúa la invitada con su respuesta.
practica.feedback: Responde solo por quienes se ofrecieron: insinúa que los demás podrían no estar de acuerdo; no habla de un equipo dividido por igual.
practica.audio: The guest said that the experiment was a success. The host asked whether everyone on the team would agree. After a pause, the guest said that those who had asked to take part certainly would. The host smiled but did not press her.
opciones: That those who did not volunteer may disagree.
That the team was split evenly over the experiment.
That the host had not understood the experiment.

practica.consigna: ¿Qué postura adopta el autor de la reseña?
practica.feedback: Reconoce el mérito del argumento («to be fair») pero discrepa de una afirmación demasiado general; no la rechaza por completo ni la acepta salvo un detalle de redacción.
practica.texto: To be fair, the guest made a strong case for flexible hours. Still, I take issue with her claim that commuting is always wasted time: many people I know use the train to read, think or switch off.
opciones: Partly persuaded, but not ready to accept such a sweeping claim.
Not persuaded by the case for flexible hours, though polite about it.
Fully persuaded, with only a small point of wording to correct.

practica.consigna: Ordena: «Su respuesta parecía dar a entender que el cambio fue difícil.»
practica.feedback: Seemed to imply + that + oración formula lo insinuado sin afirmarlo.
practica.respuesta: Her answer seemed to imply that the change was difficult

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha el episodio y escribe un resumen con una implicación y tu reacción.
evaluacion.feedback: El texto resume lo dicho con fidelidad, detecta la implicación de «not exactly», reacciona con matiz y cierra con una conclusión.
evaluacion.texto: Escucha el episodio (puedes oírlo varias veces) y escribe en inglés, de unas 180 a 260 palabras, una reseña: resume las ideas de la invitada (atribúyelas), señala una implicación, añade tu reacción con un matiz (to be fair, I would add…) y termina con una frase de cierre. No inventes datos.
evaluacion.respuesta: In this episode, the host asked her guest, a researcher, whether it is better to work from home. According to the guest, it depends. First, many people save about two hours a day because they no longer travel, and she called this a real benefit. Second, she said that some people feel lonely and hardly see their colleagues. Third, she suggested that companies could offer two office days a week, which she described as a fair compromise. When the host asked whether working at home is better, she answered that it is not exactly better, which seemed to imply that the answer is not a simple yes. What struck me was that she never said it is easy. To be fair, I found the episode balanced, and I see her point about the benefits. However, I would add one doubt of my own: two office days a week may be hard to organise for small firms, so the compromise may suit large companies better. My gut reaction was to agree with her up to a point. In short, the episode was clear and useful, and I would like to hear how companies respond.
aceptadas: This episode of the podcast was about working from home. The host asked her guest whether it is better, and the guest explained that it depends. On the positive side, many people save two hours a day because they no longer travel to an office. On the negative side, some of them feel lonely and hardly see their colleagues. She suggested that a good compromise could be two office days a week. The host asked again whether working at home is better, and the guest replied not exactly, which implied that the situation is more complicated than a simple yes or no. My reaction is positive: to be fair, she did not try to sell one answer, and what struck me was how honest she was about the problems. However, I would add that two office days a week could be hard to organise for small firms, and that could make the compromise less useful for them. Overall, I agree with her up to a point, and I would like to hear how companies respond to her ideas.
evaluacion.audio: In this week's episode, the host asked her guest, a researcher who studies remote work, whether working from home is better. The guest said that it depends. Many people, she explained, save about two hours a day because they no longer travel, and that is a real benefit. Asked whether it is therefore better, she answered: not exactly. Some people told her that they feel lonely and hardly see their colleagues. The host asked whether there is a solution, and the guest suggested, after a slight pause, that companies could offer two office days a week, which she called a fair compromise. She added that not everyone has a quiet room at home, a point that she said is often overlooked. The host thanked her and promised to return to the subject.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha el episodio y elige qué sugiere la invitada con «not exactly».
evaluacion.feedback: «Not exactly» es un no amable: da a entender que la respuesta no es un sí sencillo; no critica la pregunta ni afirma que el teletrabajo sea peor, porque después ofrece un compromiso.
evaluacion.audio: In this week's episode, the host asked her guest, a researcher who studies remote work, whether working from home is better. The guest said that it depends. Many people, she explained, save about two hours a day because they no longer travel, and that is a real benefit. Asked whether it is therefore better, she answered: not exactly. Some people told her that they feel lonely and hardly see their colleagues. The host asked whether there is a solution, and the guest suggested, after a slight pause, that companies could offer two office days a week, which she called a fair compromise. She added that not everyone has a quiet room at home, a point that she said is often overlooked. The host thanked her and promised to return to the subject.
opciones: That the answer is not as simple as yes.
That she thinks the host's question is badly phrased.
That working from home is worse than working in an office.

evaluacion.consigna: Completa: «Discrepo de su afirmación de que toda empresa debería permitir el teletrabajo.»
evaluacion.feedback: Take issue with + afirmación es la fórmula educada para discrepar de algo concreto.
evaluacion.texto: I agree with much of what the guest said, but I take ___ with her claim that every company should allow remote work.

evaluacion.consigna: ¿Qué impresión da la invitada, según el autor?
evaluacion.feedback: La invitada «came across as careful rather than evasive» porque admitió lo que la investigación no podía demostrar; la impaciencia es de la presentadora, no de ella.
evaluacion.texto: The host came across as warm but slightly impatient: she thanked the guest twice, yet she interrupted the last answer to ask about the next topic. The guest, for her part, came across as careful rather than evasive, since she admitted what the research could not show.
opciones: Careful, and honest about what her evidence could show.
Thoughtful, but not ready to admit what the research could not show.
Warm but impatient with the host's questions.

repaso.consigna: ¿Qué da a entender el autor sobre los costes para las empresas?
repaso.feedback: El autor dice que la respuesta fue larga pero sin cifras y que terminó sabiendo menos; aclara expresamente que no acusa a la invitada de ocultar nada.
repaso.texto: I liked the episode, and the guest was charming. But when the host asked about the costs to companies, the answer took four minutes and contained no number. I am not saying that she was hiding something; I am saying that I finished listening knowing less about costs than when I began.
opciones: That the guest's long answer left listeners no better informed about costs.
That the guest purposely hid the real costs from her listeners.
That the costs are too small to be worth giving a figure.

repaso.consigna: Completa: «Para ser justos, la invitada nunca dijo que todas pudieran costearlo.»
repaso.feedback: To be fair introduce un matiz a favor de la otra persona antes de seguir con la crítica.
repaso.texto: I doubt that every company can afford it. To be ___, though, the guest never said that they could, and that is a point worth remembering.

repaso.consigna: Ordena: «Yo añadiría que las empresas pequeñas podrían tener problemas con el coste.»
repaso.feedback: I would add + that introduce tu aportación sin contradecir lo dicho por otro.
repaso.respuesta: I would add that small companies may struggle with the cost

notes: Claves verificadas; distractores de escuchar/elegir reescritos como casi-aciertos; se eliminaron pistas que revelaban la clave en el audio (C88 E0 y R1, C86 P1 y R0, C90 explicación).

C87: ítems léxicos sobre variedades (sin depender de acento); C89: vocabulario B1 (take notes, a key point) sustituido por jot down y keep track of; modelo de escritura sin datos inventados; C90: modelo con aportación propia distinta de lo dicho en el audio.
Correcta única más larga en 4/33 ítems y única más corta en 0/33; español neutro (se retiró «meter baza»).
